units.title: 1. Anatomy of Spinal Cord & LMN Tract
units.sec: Anatomy of Spinal Cord & LMN Tract
units.guide:
Grey matter is horns and white matter is tracts; the ventral horn holds alpha and gamma motor neurons.
Brain-stem cranial nerve nuclei are 3-4 midbrain, 5-8 pons and 9-12 medulla, and AHC plus cranial nerve nuclei form the LMN.
The UMN vs LMN table contrasts sites, weakness patterns, tone, fasciculations and reflexes; the constituents figure numbers the LMN chain 1-7.

units.title: 2. Site of Lesion, Pathology and Radiculopathy
units.guide:
Pure motor effects arise from AHC, NMJ and muscle (myopathy); sensorimotor from root, plexus and nerve; pure sensory from ganglion.
Compressive radiculopathy is IVDP (m/c) while non-compressive radiculopathy is d/t Guillain Barre syndrome; pain is sharp, brief, lancinating and worsens with cough.
Lower limb root values pair L1 hip flexion, L2 hip adduction, L3-L4 knee extension with knee jerk, L5 ankle jerk and S1 knee flexion, hip extension and plantar flexion.

units.title: 3. Foot Drop, Upper Limb DTR Values, Neuropathy Patterns
units.sec: Foot Drop, DTR Root Values & Plexopathy Comparison
units.guide:
Common peroneal nerve gives foot drop alone; sciatic nerve adds loss of inversion; L5 radiculopathy adds loss of hip abduction and eversion.
Upper limb DTR root values: biceps jerk C5-C6, triceps jerk C6-C7, finger flexion C8-T1.
Radiculopathy (IVDP, sharp pain, both roots affected) is contrasted with plexopathy (tumour, dull deep pain, paraspinal posterior root intact); neuropathy splits into mono, multiplex and poly patterns.

units.title: 4. Polyneuropathy Types, Sensory Columns and Fibre Types
units.sec: Neuropathy Types, Sensory Columns & Nerve Fibres
units.guide:
Polyneuropathy types: sensorimotor (m/c, sensory >> motor) splits into large fibre (posterior column) and small fibre (spinothalamic + autonomic); pure sensory is ganglionopathy.
Pure motor causes are lead poisoning, dapsone and MMN-CB. Sensory columns map proprioception to A-alpha and position/fine touch/vibration/joint sense to A-beta.
Spinothalamic lateral pain is sharp-localised A-delta and dull-chronic C; temperature is C; ventral crude touch/pressure is A-beta; A-gamma is thick myelinated motor.

units.title: 5. Large vs Small Fibre Neuropathy
units.guide:
Large fibre causes: Friedreich ataxia, B12 deficiency (posterolateral cord syndrome with neuropathy), pyridoxine toxicity, taxanes. Small fibre (m/c, LADU): leprosy, amyloidosis, diabetes (m/c), uremic, vasculitis (SLE/RA/EGPA/GPA), HIV, Fabry and Tangier.
Positive symptoms: large fibre tingling/pin-and-needle/cotton wool; small fibre burning pain with stocking-glove evolution. Negative symptoms (>50% axons lost): large fibre numbness and sensory ataxia with Romberg +ve as surest sign; small fibre burns and non-healing ulcers from lost temperature sense.
Reflexes: large fibre loses DTR; small fibre DTR normal +/- ankle jerk. ANS features occur only in small fibre neuropathy.

units.title: 6. Ganglionopathy
units.guide:
Ganglionopathy is a pure sensory neuropathy/neuronopathy with large fibre and truncal involvement, arms >> legs and severe asymmetrical truncal ataxia; DTR is variable.
Causes: Sjogren's syndrome (DTR lost), anti-Hu paraneoplastic syndrome (DTR +), cisplatin, Vit B6 toxicity, HIV and thalidomide.
A separate note lists carcinomatous, vincristine and taxanes as causes of combined small + large fibre neuropathy.
